title: German Q2 GDP Revised Up to 0.3%, Ifo Business Climate Hits One-Year High
detail: Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) on August 25 revised second-quarter GDP growth up to 0.3% quarter-on-quarter (from a preliminary 0.2%) and 1.0% year-on-year (from 0.9%), driven by a rebound in exports (+2.0%) and manufacturing output (+0.9%). Separately, the Ifo Institute's business climate index rose to 88.8 in August from 86.7 in July — beating the 87.2 forecast and marking a fourth consecutive monthly increase to a one-year high. The figures mark the clearest sign yet of a turnaround after three years of near-stagnation, though the federal government still expects only 0.5% full-year 2026 growth, down from an earlier 1.0% forecast, citing energy-price pressure from the Middle East.

media.caption: German exports and manufacturing drive an upward GDP revision and a one-year-high Ifo business climate reading

title: Germany Deports 23 Afghan Men to Kabul on Charter Flight
detail: Germany deported 23 Afghan men to Kabul on a charter flight from Leipzig/Halle Airport in the early hours of August 25, escorted by federal police. Most of the men had been convicted of serious crimes including sexual offenses and bodily harm, though the government has quietly widened the policy to also remove Afghans without criminal records, per Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt. The flight brings the total to roughly 228 Afghan men returned since Chancellor Friedrich Merz took office in 2025 (some outlets reported the flight's size as closer to 30). Around 50 protesters gathered at Leipzig airport with banners reading "Stop Deportations — Refugees Welcome," while opposition lawmakers and rights groups renewed criticism of Berlin's cooperation with the Taliban regime to arrange the returns.

media.caption: Left-wing activists protest deportations at Leipzig/Halle Airport as a charter flight departs for Kabul
